uplink.description: Full port-10 uplink: battery, both outputs, onboard temperature + humidity, all three input terminals (contact + counter, 4-20 mA loop, 0-10 V), MCU temperature
uplink._note: Synthetic in-bounds TLV stream covering every recognized port-10 header. Expected values produced by running reference/upstream-codec.js (the TTN source of truth) and applying the documented vocabulary mapping: battery_voltage->battery, temperature->air.temperature, relative_humidity->air.relativeHumidity, mcu_temperature/change_output_states stay top-level, and the three input terminals become channels[] entries with zero-based labels (input0 = TEKTELIC input 1). input_1 = 1 -> input0 action.contactState 'closed'; input_1_count = 100 -> input0 pulse.count (input 1 is the only counted terminal); input_2 0x2710 = 10000 microamps -> input1 analog.current 10 mA (upstream reports the same raw count as 0.01 A); input_3 0x03E8 = 1000 mV -> input2 analog.voltage 1 V (upstream's number unchanged).

uplink.description: Temperature + humidity only (onboard climate sensor, no input field -> no channels)
uplink._note: Synthetic; expected from reference/upstream-codec.js (temperature 0x00E7=231*0.1; relative_humidity 0x55=85*0.5). No input TLV is present, so the lazily-built `channels` key is omitted entirely — the common case for this device.

uplink.description: TTN catalog example: change output states for output1 and output2
uplink._note: Commanded actuator state only: the outputs stay in the top-level `changeOutputStates` extra group (an output is not a measured position), and no `channels` key is emitted.

uplink.description: Mixed input frame: closed contact (state byte 0xFF) with counter 7, 20 mA loop current, 10 V analog input, alongside battery
uplink._note: Synthetic; expected values cross-checked against reference/upstream-codec.js, which decodes this frame as battery_voltage 3.6, input_1 = 255, input_2 = 0.02 (A), input_3 = 10 (V), input_1_count = 7. Each terminal carries a distinct top-of-range value so a swapped position would fail: the state byte is 0xFF rather than 1, proving the contact mapping is 'non-zero = closed' (the pre-channels polarity); input_2 0x4E20 = 20000 microamps -> input1 20 mA (loop at full scale); input_3 0x2710 = 10000 mV -> input2 10 V (0-10 V input at full scale). Battery stays top-level as a whole-device reading.
Synthetic; upstream returns data.error 'Couldn't find header ...' for the same input. This codec returns it via the {errors} contract instead.
